## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 56 (titled *Jotika*) governs the lighting of fires by Buddhist monastics [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a monk who kindles a fire to warm himself commits an offense that must be confessed (*pācittiya*), unless he is ill [SuttaCentral; Dhammika, Broken Buddha; Horner, Cullavagga]. In the rule's origin story, several monks built a fire on a cold winter night using an old hollow log; when a cobra nestled inside sprang out and frightened them, the Buddha promulgated the prohibition [Dhammika, Broken Buddha].
SuttaCentral records extensive parallels across canonical Vinaya traditions, including the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Pc 56), *Parivāra* (Pc 56), and corresponding rules in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Pc 137) [SuttaCentral]. Parallels survive in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions representing the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya lineages, as well as the *Upāliparipṛcchā* [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus records 659 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 121 texts, sharing extensive formulaic phrasing with other Vinaya rules such as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 57, 39, 46, and 32 [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus identifies machine alignments with Tibetan canonical Vinaya literature and commentaries, including the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2), the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104), and the *Vinayavastu* (D0001) [DharmaNexus]. An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
